title: Baby Skeleton
snippet:
Baby Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Baby Skeletons are located in the Tomb of the Giants, in the area with Pinwheel Servants, that leads to Gravelord Nito's Tomb.

title: Baby Skeleton
snippet:
Baby Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : The Baby Skeletons are able to dance with each other and form a circle if corralled into a specific spot by one of the pillars just before the second ramp underneath Nito's fog gate. It is unsure if all can be made to dance in this way but there has been records of a total of eight forming a dancing ring.
Humanity dropped by Baby Skeletons will disappear after a short duration.

title: Baby Skeleton
snippet:
Baby Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : Baby Skeletons cause Toxic build-up and tend to attack in groups. Unlike most enemies, Baby Skeletons can infinitely respawn out of the flooded ground, regardless of whether the player has rested at a bonfire or not. Given their high humanity drop rate, this trait makes them good candidates for farming humanity. Furthermore, their AI combined with their small size and slow speed causes them to run into walls and group up, making farming easy. However, their drops usually vanish extremely quickly, making it paramount to pick them up immediately after killing them. They only seem to spawn while the player is inside the water or very close to it, right next to him.

title: Baby Skeleton
snippet:
Baby Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Baby Skeletons** are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Backstep
snippet:
During the backstep, from frame 11 to 14, the player has hyperarmor, i.e. infinite poise. That means, no matter what hits the player, they will not stumble and stay on their feet. For example, the player can backstep through the boulders in Sen's Fortress without being knocked down. Keep in mind that you will still take damage, since the hyperarmor frames do not grant invincibility. The backwards ninja flip does not have hyperarmor frames.
When inputing an attack directly after the backstep, the player will perform a running attack. This can be very useful in combat, by dodging an enemy's attack with the backstep, then striking back with a running attack.

title: Backstep
snippet:
Backstep -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Backstepping is a gameplay mechanic in Dark Souls.

A backstep is performed by pressing the roll key without pressing in any direction. The player will then take a leap backwards instead of rolling.

Backstepping also grants invincibility frames, but fewer than rolling. While rolling gives 11 i-frames, backsteps only give 4. Equipping the Dark Wood Grain Ring replaces the backstep with a backwards ninja flip with 8 i-frames. This may now seem like backstepping is generally worse that rolling. However, backstepping has two situational advantages over rolling.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Balder Knights came to Lordran in large numbers along with their king, Knight King Rendal, seeking a cure for the Undead curse. However, none were able to defeat the Iron Golem, and they ended up as Hollows in the Undead Parish or Sen's Fortress.

It is possible that at least one Balder Knight managed to enter Anor Londo, becoming a member of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Balder Knights are located in the Undead Parish, and Sen's Fortress.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Balder Knights** are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : There are three varieties of Balder Knights: Side Sword, Rapier, and Crossbow. Those wielding rapiers are stronger and drop more souls.

The Rapier variant of the Balder Knight can switch stances, holding its weapon at chest level, pointed at the player. While its stance is altered thus, the Balder Knight can parry.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Several corpses of Balder knights can be found in the Undead Parish and Sen's Fortress, and are the only preplaced corpses in the game to have armor on their dead body.
Their armor has a similar design to the armor worn by Guts, the protagonist of the *Berserk* anime/manga, during its Golden Age arc.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Balder Knights have a fair amount of health, and are a considerable threat to new characters. Even one-on-one, they can be very dangerous.

Any ranged attack is useful against them, but they are fast and will close the gap quickly. Firebombs can be very useful in defeating them.

Critical attacks, such as the Parry and Riposte and Backstab, are exceedingly efficient methods to dispatch these enemies.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Ringing the bell in Quelaag's Domain first will have no different effect than if the player rang the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] first. Although this will cause Lautrec's questline to progress, leading to the death of Anastacia.
The Bells of Awakening were used to awaken Kingseeker Frampt and open the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - undead_church_bell 
 undead_church_bell : One of the Bells is located in the Undead Parish, up above from Firelink Shrine. After dispatching the Bell Gargoyles, the Chosen Undead is able to climb to the top of the Church Belltower and ring the Bell of Awakening.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : In the Prepare to Die Edition, online players in the vicinity of the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] were able to hear the bell being rung from other player worlds. This wasn’t the case for the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Bell in Quelaag’s Domain].
In the remastered version of the game, online players are now able to hear either the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] or the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s domain Bell] being rung from other player worlds while exploring one area or the other . (as the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s Bell] toll was specifically added in the remaster)

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Berenike Knights were known for their heavy armor of steel and their ultra-heavy Tower Shields forged with thick plates of iron, favoring hard defense and stability, as well as their gigantic swords capable of causing enormous damage. For their immense strength these knights were extolled as the mightiest of mighty. Among them, Black Iron Tarkus was renowned even among his fellow knights for his great strength; he wore an ultra-heavy armor made of special black iron—one with exceptional fire protection, yet so unwieldy that only he was able to wear it; his greatshield, made of the same fire-resistant material, was even heavier than that of his fellow knights.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Berenike Knights**, also known as **Heavy Knights**, are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Large and clad in the Steel Set, they wield either a large Mace or Greatsword, depending on the location where they are found, along with a Tower Shield. All Berenike Knights can be parried, but cannot be riposted.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Undead Parish — A Berenike Knight Demon can be found near the Undead Church as a miniboss guarding the Fire Keeper Soul.
Sen's Fortress — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.
Painted World of Ariamis — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. First met in Sen's Fortress, from which he relocates to Firelink Shrine, he is a merchant of advanced sorceries, including new ones upon following his questline into The Duke's Archives.

Voiced by Ian Thompson in his final role before his passing in 2022, Logan is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II* and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, although *Dark Souls II* refers to him as an unnamed "master sorcerer" due to his name being forgotten in Drangleic.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Master Logan was a famous Sorcerer and a royal member of the Vinheim Dragon School before he turned Undead about one hundred years ago. His nickname stems from the gigantic hat he wore which completely hid his face; he used it to block the noise and stares from those around him in order to focus his thoughts. His weapon was once an ordinary catalyst employed by the Sorcerers of Vinheim, but it has since been strengthened due to lengthy use over time. His sage robe, called prototype, meaning it goes back the School foundation of the Dragon School, therefore the School was founded around the times Logan was alive.

Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Big Hat Logan seems to prefer sitting down in a meditative position, except for the first encounter when he's in a hanging jail cage.
If you get the Man-Serpent leaning against the wall next to the cage he is in, It will break, meaning you don't need to get the boulder trap to break it, with careful planning.
Logan shares many similarities with Sage Freke from *Demon's Souls*. Both are first found trapped in cages and rescued by the player. Both are preceded by apprentices looking for them, have an unhealthy fascination with magic, and are found sitting in the main hub area.
Rickert of Vinheim mentions to the player that Big Hat Logan is famous in Vinheim; however, he also mentions that Logan was from "a hundred years ago". Either Logan has remained sane for as long as he has been undead, or time warping in Lordran has brought Logan to a time where one does not belong.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
When Logan is encountered hostile, he is not hollowed, but was driven insane in a more "traditional" sense. All other NPCs appear in their charred, undead forms when they attack players after hollowing.
If the player dies fighting against Big Hat Logan while in Seath's arena, the player will respawn in the prison as if they were killed by Seath himself, which underlines that Logan became just as mad as Seath.
Logan's Tin Crystallization Catalyst is actually 結晶の錫杖 ("Crystall Staff"). 錫杖 (khakkhara), is a ringed staff used by Buddhist monks. This implies that Logan venerated Seath as a God.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - locations 
 locations : #Caged in Sen's Fortress behind a destructible wall (can be broken by a Serpent Soldier, a strong weapon, or rolling a boulder down the middle groove).
#Prison in the Duke's Archives.
#Library in the Duke's Archives, near the room leading to the Crystal Cave.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Big Hat Logan is first encountered in Sen's Fortress. His cage is hidden behind a wall, which can be destroyed by manipulating the iron ball trap mechanism, using a powerful enough weapon, or goading the sleeping man-serpent guard to attack the wall. After freeing him with either the Cage Key or Master Key, Big Hat Logan thanks the player and later retreats to Firelink Shrine. There, he accompanies Griggs of Vinheim and offers to sell the player advanced Sorceries.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

He is also the creator of Homing Soulmass, a sinister spell similar to Pursuers and therefore closer to dark sorceries, which enlights a more shady side of Logan. Griggs affirms that Logan has not concern for others, and that he is an unreasonable and troublesome man.

In his attempt to reach Anor Londo, presumably to gain access to The Duke's Archives and its vast store of endless knowledge, he became imprisoned in Sen's Fortress, where he first encounters the Chosen Undead.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - wares 
 wares : Logan will not sell anything to the player unless they have at least 15 Intelligence.

Only available at The Duke's Archives

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : Big Hat's Set and Logan's Catalyst are found in a chest where he normally sits in The Duke's Archives after he goes insane and travels to the arena where Seath is first encountered. (The elevator is likely at the top of its shaft and the lever will need to be used to bring it back. It is recessed and hidden on the first floor.) The player must kill Logan then trigger a loading screen (either by logging out or using a Homeward Bone) to make the chest appear.
When Big Hat Logan is battled, he wears no clothes except for his big hat, because he has gone insane.
When spoken to in the Duke's Archives there is no Intelligence requirement to purchase his spells.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan soon leaves Firelink Shrine after the Lordvessel has been obtained. He is then jailed in The Duke's Archives. Logan explains that he is there to study Seath the Scaleless and his magic. After freeing him with the Archive Tower Giant Cell Key, players can find Logan in an ancillary library close to the third bonfire in The Duke's Archives, where he sells Crystal Sorceries as well as his prior spells. Alternatively, if not freed by you by Seath's defeat, he will free himself and move to the library.

Unfortunately, Logan's infatuation with Seath's magic eventually drives him insane after Seath has been defeated and his entire stock of spells has been purchased. Speaking with him again, after the above conditions are met, will cause him to move to the large chamber where Seath the Scaleless was first encountered and become hostile.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - theory 
 theory : Given Logan's obsession with Seath and his Archives, it's possible that he let himself be captured by the Serpent Men in order to reach The Duke's Archives easily, as the two locations we find him jailed yet not much concerned are the Archives and Sen's fortress, areas crowd by Serpent Men.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Big Hat Logan has a repertoire of dangerous Sorceries, including Soul Spear and Homing Soulmass. If attacked later in the game, he also possesses their augmented crystal variants. However, he is fairly fragile and can be killed before he deals too much damage.

If killed when encountered in Sen's Fortress or Firelink Shrine, he will **not** drop anything.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet: Many millennia past his demise, Knight Slayer Tsorig found the black iron armor and shield of the deceased Tarkus, and made them his own. The black set would gain notoriety as an omen of the feared Knight Slayer, a display of the terrible strength of one with the vigor to wear it.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet:
Black Iron Tarkus -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Black Iron Tarkus is the strongest of the Berenike Knights. Berenike Knights were known for their heavy armor of steel and their ultra-heavy Tower Shields forged with thick plates of iron, favoring hard defense and stability, as well as their gigantic swords capable of causing enormous damage. For their immense strength these knights were extolled as the mightiest of mighty. Tarkus was renowned even among his fellow knights for his great strength; he wore an ultra-heavy armor made of special black iron—one with exceptional fire protection, yet so unwieldy that only he was able to wear it; his greatshield, made of the same fire-resistant material, was even heavier than that of his fellow knights.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet:
Tarkus was seen sitting in Firelink Shrine in the debut trailer as a non-playable character, but in the game he is simply a white phantom.
Black Iron Tarkus is likely a reference to the antagonist knight Tarkus from the 1987 manga *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure* who himself is named after the 1971 progressive rock album by Emerson, Lake, & Palmer. Both characters are massive knights with enormous, seemingly unwieldy weapons and thick armor. The way Black Iron Tarkus dies is also similar to how Tarkus from the manga falls off a cliff and into a barrack, though the latter survives the fall.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet:
Black Iron Tarkus -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : In a tower structure at the end of the walkway to the right from where the fog door to the Iron Golem is located. Like other summon signs, Tarkus's summon sign is only visible if the player has not put down a summon sign and is in human form. He aids the player in taking on the Iron Golem as a white phantom. He is notoriously tough and can serve as a distraction during the battle. In fact, Tarkus can defeat the boss all by himself in the first playthrough and stands a break-even chance of doing so on future playthroughs with minimal support from the player. A Black Iron Set is found on his corpse in Anor Londo, next to the entrance to the Painted World of Ariamis. A Painting Guardian stands next to his corpse, possibly removing it from the room since the body is so far away from the entrance.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, after a grueling and lengthy ordeal, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet:
Black Iron Tarkus -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Many players favor Black Iron Tarkus due to his immense strength, his reliability in PvP and his ability to fight the Iron Golem with minimal support.
Tarkus is also the Estonian word for "wisdom".
Even though it says that Tarkus's armor was unwieldy to all but Tarkus himself, when summoned for the fight against the Iron Golem, he "fat rolls" due to not having enough Endurance.
Tarkus was seen sitting in Firelink Shrine in the debut trailer as a non-playable character, but in the game he is simply a white phantom.

title: Black Iron Tarkus
snippet:
Black Iron Tarkus -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Black Iron Tarkus**, (黒鉄のタルカス *Kurogane no Tarukasu*) also referred to as **Iron Tarkus**, is a character and summon-able white phantom in *Dark Souls*. He can be summoned by the player in the fight against the Iron Golem boss in Sen's Fortress.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - locations 
 locations : With the exception of the final area, Black Knights are unique enemies that do not respawn. They can be found in the following locations throughout Lordran:
One Black Knight Sword wielder in the Undead Burg - Guarding the Blue Tearstone Ring.
One Black Knight Greatsword wielder in Undead Parish - Atop the tower near the locked gate.
Two Black Knight Sword wielders in the Northern Undead Asylum, when revisited. - Guarding the Peculiar Doll and the other at the opposite end of the long hallway beyond the second bonfire originally encountered.
One Black Knight Halberd wielder in Darkroot Basin - Guarding the Grass Crest Shield.
One Black Knight Greataxe wielder in The Catacombs - Through a crumbling floor.
One Black Knight Halberd wielder in the Tomb of the Giants - Guarding the Effigy Shield.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : It is usually not a good idea to take on Black Knights directly, as they have high Poise and can deal huge amounts of damage. Their attacks are slow, however, meaning that they are susceptible to backstabs and parries.

It's also advisable for lower level players to try and force them off ledges if possible (such as Undead Burg small bridge near bonfire or Darkroot Basin cliff) if killing them becomes problematic. This can either kill them or open them for a plunging attack to rack up some serious damage. One could also position themselves in front of a ledge, roll behind the knight as it attacks, and backstab it to knock it over the edge. If the knight dies from the fall, item drops will still be added to the players inventory like they would if the knight was killed normally.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : In *Dark Souls: The Age of Fire*, it is revealed that the Black Knight in the Northern Undead Asylum is actually what remains of the protagonist of the comic series, Silver Knight Arkon.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Black Knights** are powerful enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
One Black Knight Greataxe wielder in The Catacombs - Through a crumbling floor.
One Black Knight Halberd wielder in the Tomb of the Giants - Guarding the Effigy Shield.
Five respawn at the Kiln of the First Flame and include all variations, two of which are sword wielders, and one of each of the other weapon wielders.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Black Knights are encountered, individually, in many areas of the game as non-respawning challenges for players. At the Kiln of the First Flame, however, they do respawn.

They wield various slow hitting but powerful weapons, the Black Knight Shield and wear the Black Knight Set.

title: Black Knight
snippet: Attacking them from where they cannot reach or where they will not attack the player will make it easy to kill the knights with ranged attacks, such as bows or firebombs.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Black Knights were once the proud Silver Knights of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Long ago they fought chaos demons and were charred black, also giving them high Fire resistance. Many traveled with Lord Gwyn to the Kiln of the First Flame, and were burned to ashes when he linked the First Flame, wandering the world as disembodied spirits ever after. Their disembodied spirits can be seen roaming the stairs descending into the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Bone Tower

 location : Found in the Tomb of the Giants.

title: Bone Tower
snippet:
Bone Tower -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : Bone Towers are intimidating enemies that tend to ambush the player, concealing themselves in the ground until the player draws near. They are slow to approach and attack by either extending their many limbs and spinning, or smashing their tower of bones onto the ground. They usually attack in small groups, but do not have very high HP.

snippet:
Bottomless Box -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : It can be purchased from Domhnall of Zena located in the Depths (until both bells are rung) for 1,000 souls. He can be found sitting between the way to the Gaping Dragon and the entrance to Blighttown. Since Patch 1.05, it can also be purchased from the Undead Male Merchant located in the Undead Burg for 1,000 souls.

title: Bottomless Box
snippet:
Bottomless Box -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : A peculiar bottomless wooden box. Its origins are unknown. Some deride it as a symbol of unbrideled avarice.

Any number of items can be deposited into the box, and items can be managed while resting at a Bonfire.

title: Bottomless Box
snippet:
Bottomless Box -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : As the name and description says, the Bottomless Box is a box that can hold an unlimited number of items. The items can be retrieved again from any other Bonfire. It works like Stockpile Thomas from *Demon's Souls*. However, unlike Stockpile Thomas, it does not separate every item and weapon type, and instead offers different tabs for consumables, upgrade materials, weapons, armor, ammunition, and rings.

The Bottomless Box cannot store souls. It can only be accessed and managed while the player is resting at a bonfire. This limits its utility to that of inventory management.

title: Cage Key
snippet:
Cage Key -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : The Cage key can open several cages in Sen's Fortress:
The cage that Big Hat Logan is locked in.
A cage that contains a Soul of a Hero in the same area that Big Hat Logan is in.
The cage that can be used as an elevator to move through Sen's Fortress.
The Master Key can open every openable cage, except the Cage Elevator.

title: Cage Key

title: Cage Key

 description : Key to the hanging cage in Sen's Fortress.

If a hapless adventurer becomes fatigued during an imprudent attempt to overcome the fortress, the serpent men will not kill him, but lock him up in a lonely cage. Eventually, unless they have forgotten, they drag the victim off to who-knows-where.

title: Carvings

title: Covetous Gold Serpent Ring
snippet:
Covetous Gold Serpent Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - availability 
 availability : The ring is found in Sen's Fortress. There is a two story stairwell in the fortress with boulders running down it. If the player follows it they will reach a dead end hallway. Near the end of the hallway there is a room with a Mimic in it which players may stand in to stay out of the path of the rocks, and a deep pit at the end of the hallway. After three boulders pile up, the fourth will run over the filled in pit and destroy the wall, opening up a new room holding the ring. Be careful to move out of the way after grabbing the ring, as the boulders will continue to roll through the room and potentially kill the player.

title: Covetous Gold Serpent Ring
snippet:
Covetous Gold Serpent Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : The Covetous Gold Serpent Ring increases Item Discovery by 200. It does *not* stack with the Symbol of Avarice. Along with the Symbol of Avarice, the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring is one of the only items to increase item drop chance.

The ring is invaluable for hunting down upgrade materials for weapon and armor reinforcement, as well as rare items such as the Channeler's Trident.

title: Symbol of Avarice
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Symbol of Avarice is a head piece that possesses high physical defense and Poise, but low fire and lightning resistance; in addition, it cannot be upgraded and drains HP at the rate of 5 per second while being worn. In exchange, however, it gives a +200 Item Discovery to the player and increases souls obtained by 20%, effectively combining the soul absorption increase with the effect of the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring and ten liquid humanity.

Due to its heaviness and constant health drain, the Symbol of Avarice is impractical for serious combat; however, it is good for soul farming or even item farming if the player has no free ring slots or has not acquired the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

The Symbol of Avarice's effects does not stack with the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

title: Balder Side Sword
snippet:
Balder Side Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - availability 
 availability : The Balder Side Sword is dropped by Balder Knights that wield it the Undead Parish and Sen's Fortress at a 1% drop rate.

Since the drop rate is low, using the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring or Symbol of Avarice and 10 liquid Humanity to get to 410 Item Discovery is recommended. As the sword is available long before any of the item discovery boosting gear, it is preferable to use a substitute weapon until the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring is obtained to avoid incredibly lengthy grinding.

title: Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : The Symbol of Avarice is a potential drop from all Mimics encountered throughout the course of the game. It may even be obtained from the very first Mimic in the High Wall of Lothric. All Mimics have guaranteed drops, but they may also yield a Symbol of Avarice along with these.

Since Mimics are non-respawning enemies, each encounter with one is very valuable if one is looking to obtain a Symbol of Avarice. The player must first make sure their Item Discovery attribute is as high as possible. Crushing a Rusted Coin, or even a Rusted Gold Coin, before engaging a Mimic is recommended, as well as equipping the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

title: Man-serpent Greatsword
snippet:
Man-serpent Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Unlike the other greatswords, the Man-serpent Greatsword is extremely stat-efficient due to its lack of Dexterity requirement or scaling, quickly outdamaging the Claymore and Bastard Sword, especially when two-handed. This, combined with its relatively fast attack speed and long range, makes it ideal for Strength/Faith or Strength/Intelligence builds.

Its only real downside is its sheer rarity, and it is recommended to wear the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring when grinding for this weapon. To be of the most use, the player must also have invested little to nothing in Dexterity.

title: Shield of Want
snippet: The Shield of Want's most notable feature is that it boosts the soul gain of the wielder, granting 20% more souls when defeating any enemy, including bosses and other players. It fully stacks with other soul-boosting accessories, such as the Symbol of Avarice and Covetous Silver Serpent Ring, and can even stack with itself should a second Shield of Want be wielded in the opposite hand.

title: Man Serpent Summoner
snippet:
Summoners can notice you if you are under the effect of the hidden body sorcery, though they are still affected by Spook/the slumbering dragoncrest ring.
The summoners can be used for farming souls. The Drakeblood Knights they summon each yield 4,000 souls upon defeat (an amount that can be increased by equipping items that give more souls to the player, like the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring, the Shield of Want and the Symbol of Avarice) and they will always spawn at the same spot. The player just needs to wait for them by standing behind of their spawning location, receive them with a backstab and then finish them off.
An excellent place to farm the mendicant's staff that they wield is the Great Belfry bonfire: one is across the hall from said bonfire with its back to you.

snippet:
Ruin Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - availability 
 availability : Drops from the five Ruin Sentinels located just past the King's Gate bonfire in Drangleic Castle. Drop rate is low and the enemies are few, meaning the player will likely have to farm to get even a single piece.
**For maximum efficiency, wearing the Jester's Cap, Prisoner's Tatters, Covetous Gold Serpent Ring, Watchdragon Parma and using Rusted Coins is advised.
**As with all respawning enemies, one can join the Company of Champions to make the Sentinels respawn indefinitely.

title: Soul
snippet:
Soul -  Dark Souls - mechanic - souls_from_enemies 
 souls_from_enemies : Almost all enemies drop souls. How many are dropped depends on the enemy type, the current difficulty level (the higher the NG+, the more souls), and whether or not the player overkilled the opponent (dealing more than 150% of an enemy’s total HP in one hit).

Overkilling enemies grants around 20% more souls per kill. It is possible to further boost the amount of souls gained from killing enemies by wearing the Symbol of Avarice and/or the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring. The maximum percentage of souls attainable is 172.8% per kill.

title: Symbol of Avarice
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice -  Dark Souls - armor - availability 
 availability : Dropped by Mimics. This item can be obtained with a higher chance if the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring is equipped and 10 liquid humanity is absorbed. As of patch 1.05, if the player kills all of the Mimics in the game, the Symbol of Avarice will be a guaranteed drop from the last one killed. The Mimic in Oolacile Township is not included in this, as it is not part of the base game.

title: Chaos Eater
snippet:
Chaos Eater -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Despite having multiple eyes, it is still possible to sneak up behind them.
Falling or using a plunging attack on the ones tied to Siegmeyer's questline will result in them eating the player as if they were grabbed. It can be escaped in the same way as if being normally grabbed.
They are the only way in the game to farm Red Titanite Slabs, although due to its extremely low drop rate, using Humanity or a Covetous Gold Serpent Ring is recommended.
The Chaos Eater vaguely resembles the transcended Kushan Emperor from Berserk.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - farming 
 farming : Since Drakeblood Knights spawn infinitely and yield a base amount of 4,000 souls, they can be used for farming. By equipping the Symbol of Avarice, the Shield of Want, the Hornet Ring, the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring, and the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring (and perhaps also Aldrich's Ruby to alleviate some of the HP drain produced by the Symbol of Avarice), the player can maximize the amount of souls acquired for each knight killed.

The player just needs to stand behind their spawning spot and begin combat with a backstab, the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring will ensure they don't turn hostile prematurely and the Hornet Ring will increase the damage dealt, allowing the player to kill them with only a few more hits. Each knight defeated will yield 7,000+ souls and the process can be repeated as many times as necessary.

title: Jester's Cap
snippet:
Jester's Cap -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Raises item discovery, work in conjunction with Prisoner's Tatters, Covetous gold serpent ring, Watchdragon parma, and Rusted Coin.

title: Covetous Silver Serpent Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
**Found in the Undead Settlement, near the two Evangelists and the Demon. From the Evangelists, walk outside and drop down to the roof on the right. The ring is on a corpse by the chimney.
***Covetous Silver Serpent Ring +3** (*The Ringed City*)
**Found in The Dreg Heap, soon after meeting the first two Lothric Knights. Go right, into the building where several Murkmen will spawn and you can find the Murky Longstaff. The wall in front of the corpse holding the staff is an illusory wall. Go through the area it hides, until the place where the Great Soul Dregs is. From here, fall down to a ledge to find the ring.

title: Kirk, Knight of Thorns
snippet:
Kirk, Knight of Thorns -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : One of the promotional pictures for Kirk features him invading a player in New Londo Ruins; however, he never invades there in-game.
It is entirely possible for Kirk to drop both his sword and shield in a single encounter. Equipping the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring will boost the chances further, and aid players in obtaining his equipment in a single playthrough.
